newsitem.title: GERMANY: BHF-Bank 96 profit falls, dividend steady.
newsitem.headline: BHF-Bank 96 profit falls, dividend steady.

text.p: Germany's BHF-Bank AG on Tuesday reported a five percent decline in operating profit for 1996 amid heavy pressure on its lending business and from its involvement with the AGIV group.
The second-tier German bank said it had been forced to dig into its hidden reserves to secure an unchanged dividend payout of 1.45 marks per share for the year.
"1996 was an extremely difficult year for the bank, although lasting improvements were achieved in important areas," said BHF's new chairman Ernst Michel Kruse in a statement.
BHF reported operating profits after provisions of 358 million marks, down from 377 million the previous year.
The bank said its involvement with struggling industrial holding company AGIV, of which it owns just less than 50 percent, had shaved 109 million marks off its earnings.

BHF said it remained keen to cut down its industrial holdings, but supported AGIV's efforts to restructure its business. These efforts had priority over any change in its ownership structure, BHF said.
Engineering group Metallgesellschaft AG earlier this year pulled out of what had appeared to be advanced talks to take over BHF's AGIV holding.

Increased lending risks forced BHF to add 233 million marks to its bad debt provisions in 1996. Net risk provisions rose to 185 million marks from 107 million in 1995, lifted by returns from securities held in BHF's liquidity portfolio.

However the bank noted that its earnings on core banking business had improved. Net interest income rose four percent to 777 million marks and net commission income increased 11 percent to 461 million marks.
BHF also announced further changes to its management board structure, following this month's earlier-than-expected departure of chief executive Wolfgang Strutz in favour of Kruse.

Board members Wulf von Schimmelmann and Gernot Reiners are to leave the board, by mutual agreement with BHF, on March 31 while Tilo Paduch will join the board, taking responsibility for corporate banking.
